fact_check_verdict: Independently verified acquisition, training, hardware and planned studies. Methods example is explicitly editorial and conditional.

claims.spoken: UAA announced the equipment acquisition on September 9th.
The University of Alaska Anchorage AI and Robotics Lab acquired it.
requires: Expand UAA before relying on abbreviation in narration.

claims.spoken: The device is a Wearable Sensing DSI-24 dry EEG.
requires: An EEG records signals. No thought symbols or clinical result.

claims.spoken: The Educational Legacy Fund funded the equipment.
requires: Credit funding only. No price is reported.

claims.spoken: Faculty and students received equipment training.
requires: Observed milestone. The research studies remain planned.

claims.spoken: Vadim Egorov is a graduate student.
requires: Use a generic student illustration, not an invented portrait.

claims.spoken: Egorov viewed his recorded electrical signals.
requires: Demonstration is observed. Any trace drawn here is schematic.
Cross-checked against UAA. Literal sensors must number exactly19.

claims.spoken: Egorov usually works with public EEG datasets.
requires: Public datasets remain valuable, not displaced.

claims.spoken: Egorov anticipates collecting recordings for his own tasks.
requires: Added collection capability, not a newly granted right to choose research.

claims.spoken: UAA plans cognitive-state research during reading.
requires: Use planned in narration and large planned label on this scene.

claims.spoken: Another planned project studies brain activity during programming.
requires: Programming, not AI-assisted coding. Use planned framing.

claims.spoken: The programming project also plans to track eye movements.
requires: Separate proposed eye tracking, not EEG alone reading eyes.

claims.spoken: The announcement describes planned studies rather than completed findings.
requires: No model output, accuracy, sample count or completed dataset.

claims.spoken: A claim about new people requires evaluation on people absent from training.
requires: Editorial conditional methods principle. No allegation of UAA leakage and no invented UAA protocol.

claims.spoken: The device records electrical activity using sensors that rest directly against the scalp.
requires: Research equipment, not medical diagnosis. Traces labeled SCHEMATIC and not actual UAA recordings.
claims.additional_source_locator: DSI-24 User Manual section2.4, printed page11, dry electrode-tip contact with the scalp; verified2026-09-12.

pre_storyboard_status: Final narration cites all16 approved distinct facts. No completed-study result is claimed.
